newsitem.title: USA: Gaylord Q4 hurt by pricing, inflation.
newsitem.headline: Gaylord Q4 hurt by pricing, inflation.

text.p: Gaylord Container Corp said operating earnings for the September 30 fourth quarter decreased by about $81 million due to lower product prices.

The quarter also was hurt by general inflation and higher group insurance costs, the company said. The combination of lower prices and higher costs was partly offset by higher volume and lower fiber cost primarily due to lower old corrugated container prices, which increased operating earnings.

Gaylord posted a fourth-quarter loss of $0.17 per share compared with a year-ago profit of $1 per share. The current period results include a $4.7 million after-tax charge related to staff reduction and a $600,000 or $0.01 per share extraordinary loss on early retirement of debt.

During fiscal 1996, the company reduced debt to $634.4 million from $687.1 million. Gaylord's mill division set a production record in the fiscal year despite about 80,000 tons of market downtime and after adjusting for an extra week in fiscal 1996, producing more than 1.5 million tons. Corrugated shipments were up eight percent to a record 13.3 billion square feet.
